storyboard.claim: The 'rules as survival' reading is an outsider misconception that Reynolds actively tears apart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will in a thinking pose — the protagonist processing an argument being made about his world.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Direct pushback on the previous beat's 'immune system' framing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names Reynolds as the author making a deliberate authorial argument, not just depicting events.

storyboard.claim: The rules are not a survival mechanism — they are a suicide pact.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The numbered rules list on screen — the very object being re-labeled as a death sentence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Direct rebuttal to the 'survival mechanism' frame from context beats.
storyboard.addedInformation: The word 'suicide pact' reframes the rules from protective code to guaranteed death contract.

storyboard.claim: Rule 3 creates an infinite revenge loop — there is no exit condition.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will in a worried, thinking pose — trapped inside a loop he cannot think his way out of.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the logical proof that the rules are self-defeating.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the 'infinite loop' is argued in narration; staging conveys worry but not the geometric inevitability.

storyboard.claim: The other side is equally obligated by the same rule — the loop never closes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-node flow diagram showing the kill obligation cycling back on itself.
storyboard.onScreenText: You kill → They must kill → You must kill again
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the logical argument started in i=42 with a visual proof.
storyboard.addedInformation: The diagram makes the abstract loop structurally visible.

storyboard.claim: It is a mathematical certainty that nobody survives — the machine only makes bodies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Shawn alone collapsed — the undeniable output of the machine: one dead body.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The logical conclusion of the flow diagram: the output is death.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shawn's collapsed body embodies the outcome the flow diagram predicts.

storyboard.claim: The rules are an autoimmune disease — the community destroying itself from inside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped — the body language of someone being consumed from within.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the 'perpetual motion machine' metaphor from i=44 as biology.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slump shows internal collapse, not external attack — matching the autoimmune concept.

storyboard.claim: The autoimmune metaphor flips the entire frame — a genuine realization moment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will surprised — the face of a concept landing hard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The reaction shot after the autoimmune disease metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: this is conversational acknowledgment — staging conveys the realization but content is thin.

callout.text: Looking at it like a shield

storyboard.claim: The narrator admits they had been seeing the rules as protection — a view now rejected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will holding a shield — the old wrong frame, visually struck through.
storyboard.onScreenText: Looking at it like a shield
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narrator's confession that they held the 'immune system' misconception from context beats.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike callout signals this framing is being discarded, not endorsed.

storyboard.claim: Will believes the rules will heal him — but this belief is the error.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will blank and idle — believing he is taking medicine when he is taking poison.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the 'wrong frame' lesson from i=47 to Will's specific psychology.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike callout signals Will is wrong — the narration corrects his belief immediately after.

storyboard.claim: Will is not the shooter — he is the bullet loading himself into the gun that killed Shawn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gun icon with Will afraid — he is the next round in the chamber.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the medicine metaphor: what Will thinks is a cure is the weapon that killed his brother.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phrase 'same gun' links Will's fate to Shawn's death — the icon makes it literal.

storyboard.claim: The rules convert terrifying randomness into a manageable to-do list — a false scaffold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will afraid and thinking — trying to process chaos through the rules' false order.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the psychological mechanism that makes the rules feel necessary.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explains why Will adopts the rules despite their fatal logic — randomness is the real terror.

storyboard.claim: Step 1, Step 2, Step 3 — the rules convert the moral weight of murder into a checklist.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rules list on screen — the numbered steps that make murder feel like procedure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes concrete what 'false sense of control' looks like as a script.
storyboard.addedInformation: The word 'tradition' shifts moral responsibility from Will to the code — the rules grant absolution.

storyboard.claim: Will steps into the elevator on the eighth floor — the descent begins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The floor counter showing 8, Will walking in — the countdown clock starting.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from analysis back to the story — the physical act that sets the plot in motion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Floor 8 is the starting point; the elevator will count down to L (lobby) over the entire book.

storyboard.claim: The elevator is metallic and trapping; the world went dark the night Shawn died.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will afraid in the elevator room — surrounded by the metal box that traps him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Establishes the sensory texture of the elevator space after entering it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blacked-out moon marks cosmic abandonment — the universe went dark with Shawn's death.

storyboard.claim: The elevator's claustrophobia functions as a pressure cooker — sealed, building heat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will worried in the elevator — the space itself exerting its force on him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds analytical frame to the sensory description from i=53.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: 'pressure cooker' is a narrator metaphor — staging conveys the trapped feeling but not the mechanism.

storyboard.claim: An elevator strips all agency — you press a button and you are fully at the machine's mercy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will blank and still in the elevator — the posture of someone who can only wait.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens the pressure-cooker frame: not only sealed, but powerless.
storyboard.addedInformation: The elevator is chosen by Reynolds to literalize Will's surrender to the rules' logic.

storyboard.claim: Once the doors close, Will and the reader are trapped together with the weight of a fatal mistake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will afraid in the elevator — reader and character sealed inside together.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The doors closing completes the trap that i=55 described.
storyboard.addedInformation: The narration addresses the reader directly — implicating them in Will's descent.

storyboard.claim: Eight floors, sixty seconds, zero exits — the parameters of an inescapable space.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The floor counter — the countdown made visible; eight floors left.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the countdown its exact numbers after establishing the trap.
storyboard.addedInformation: The three constraints (floors, seconds, exits) make the trap precise and measurable.

storyboard.claim: The narrators were physically breathless reading — the reader cannot look away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will in the elevator — the space that holds the reader as tightly as it holds Will.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reader-response confirmation after the countdown parameters from i=57.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: this is conversational narrator reaction — no new story content.

storyboard.claim: Will describes Shawn's death as an earthquake — the ground opening up and swallowing him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will falling — the physical sensation of the ground giving way beneath him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Bridges the elevator's physical claustrophobia to the original trauma of Shawn's murder.
storyboard.addedInformation: The earthquake metaphor links Shawn's death to the elevator's downward motion.

storyboard.claim: Going down floor by floor — the elevator is a literal and metaphorical descent into the underworld.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will standing blank in the elevator as it descends — the container of the underworld journey.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Fuses the earthquake sensation from i=59 with the elevator's downward mechanics.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: 'underworld' is the narrator's mythological frame, forbidden from visual staging by the story bible.

callout.text: Leaving the land of the living

storyboard.claim: Will walks away from the world of the living — Shawn, already dead, waits below.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will walking in the elevator alongside Shawn — the living descending toward the dead.
storyboard.onScreenText: Leaving the land of the living
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the descent from i=60 its human geography: the living floor and the dead space below.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shawn present frames the destination — Will walks toward where the dead already are.

storyboard.claim: The elevator is a purgatory — a supernatural space between the living and the dead.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will and Shawn side by side in the elevator — the living and the dead sharing one small space.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the in-between quality of the elevator after establishing it as the underworld's doorstep.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two generations — living boy, dead brother — in the same metal box makes the purgatory concrete.

storyboard.claim: Will is suspended in liminal space — his soul's destination still undecided.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will alone, blank, and still — suspended between two fates.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows the purgatory frame to Will's individual soul — his decision is what the space waits for.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: 'liminal space' and 'soul's destination' are framing — the concrete story fact is Will hasn't decided yet.

storyboard.claim: The purgatory frame is wrong because this elevator is active, not passive — Will is being tried, not waiting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will with a neutral face — the struck callout rejecting the passive reading.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Direct rebuttal to the purgatory frame from i=62 and i=63.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike signals the narrator is correcting the other host's framing, not endorsing it.

storyboard.claim: Classic purgatory means you sit and wait for God to act on you — that is not this book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will blank and still — illustrating the passive purgatory model being argued against.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Elaborates what 'too much passivity' means — defining the purgatory model before rejecting it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The definition sets up the contrast: Will is not waiting for a verdict — the ghosts are forcing one.

storyboard.claim: This is not passive — the elevator is active, aggressive. Will is not acted upon.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will angry and pointing — the force and intent of the space, not a passive waiting room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The counter-argument: the elevator is a place of active confrontation, not passive waiting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the 'acted upon' description — Will is an agent being challenged, not a subject being judged.

storyboard.claim: Will is on the witness stand — the ghosts aren't company, they are interrogating him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Law icon + Will worried with Shawn beside him — the courtroom dynamic made visible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the passive purgatory frame with an active courtroom frame.
storyboard.addedInformation: The courtroom reframe explains why the ghosts appear: they are not consoling Will, they are prosecuting him.

storyboard.claim: Will barely speaks — he is mostly stunned and staring. It doesn't look like a standard cross-examination.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will alone, blank, and silent — the witness who gives no verbal testimony.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A pushback on the witness-stand frame: Will's silence makes it look less like a courtroom.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the tension between the 'trial' frame and Will's silence is the hosts debating — no new story fact.

storyboard.claim: Will is physically stunned — sweat, stare — not a defensive witness arguing back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will afraid and still — the body language of shock, not resistance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives concrete physical detail for why the standard cross-examination frame doesn't fit.
storyboard.addedInformation: The stunned, sweating body is how Will receives the ghosts — his silence is shock, not strategy.

storyboard.claim: His beliefs — not his voice — are on trial. The intention to commit murder is itself the testimony.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Law icon + Will blank — his stated voice is absent but his intent fills the courtroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Resolves the tension from i=68/69: Will doesn't need to speak because his intent speaks for him.
storyboard.addedInformation: This reframe resolves the apparent contradiction — the trial is of the rules' logic, not Will's voice.

storyboard.claim: The entire supernatural trial exists to prosecute the code — the rules themselves are on the stand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rules list with Shawn pointing — the ghost witnesses targeting the code, not the boy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Synthesizes the trial frame: the defendant is not Will but the inherited code he carries.
storyboard.addedInformation: This reframe elevates the stakes — the book is not about one revenge, it is about dismantling a system.

storyboard.claim: The elevator stops at floor 7. The first ghost witness is called: Buck.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The floor counter showing 7, Buck and Will in the elevator — the trial's first witness entering.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the courtroom frame into action — the first witness materializes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Floor 7 is the first stop in the countdown — each floor brings a new ghost and a new piece of evidence.

storyboard.claim: Nobody is there — then a match is struck. Smoke fills the small space. Buck arrives through fire.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fire icon with Buck blank in the elevator — the literal flame that announces his ghost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The physical moment of Buck's arrival, following the floor-stop announcement in i=72.
storyboard.addedInformation: The match and smoke are Buck's signature — sensory details that make his ghostly entrance physical.

storyboard.claim: Buck appears wearing the exact shirt he died in — his death is worn on his body.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck blank in the elevator, his death-day clothes visible — a ghost dressed in his final moment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names and grounds Buck after his smoke-arrival in i=73.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shirt as death marker: Reynolds makes Buck's murder visible before a word is spoken.

storyboard.claim: Thick smoke in the tiny unventilated metal box — the sensory detail is overwhelming.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will afraid beside Buck in the elevator — two people in an impossibly small space filling with smoke.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the sensory texture of Buck's arrival — the smoke is physically present.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smoke in the enclosed box intensifies the claustrophobia already established in i=54/55/56.

storyboard.claim: Buck turns and shows Will the bullet holes in his shirt — front and back — proof of how he died.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck afraid, pointing at his own chest — the wounds visible, his death-testimony literal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Buck's first act is to exhibit his death — making his murder viscerally real to Will.
storyboard.addedInformation: Front and back bullet holes mean he was shot through — the detail signals ambush or close-range violence.

storyboard.claim: Buck represents inherited trauma — violence and the rules passed down like family heirlooms.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Inheritance icon with Buck — the estate metaphor made literal: trauma as an estate passed to heirs.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lifts from the physical detail of bullet holes to the systemic meaning Buck carries.
storyboard.addedInformation: The inheritance frame recontextualizes Buck: he is not just a dead man, he is a link in a chain of transmission.

storyboard.claim: Buck taught Shawn the rules, gave Shawn the gun. Shawn is dead. Will now carries that same gun.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gun icon, Will and Buck in the elevator — the inheritance made visible as a single weapon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the inheritance from i=77 concrete: the heirloom is literally the gun in Will's waistband.
storyboard.addedInformation: Three names, one gun: Buck → Shawn → Will. The chain of custody is the chain of death.

callout.text: Baton pass in a relay race

storyboard.claim: The gun passes hand to hand like a baton in the worst relay race — each runner dies at the finish.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck reaching toward Will — the gesture of passing the baton, the inheritance in motion.
storyboard.onScreenText: Baton pass in a relay race
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the three-person chain from i=78 as a relay: the baton keeps running even as runners fall.
storyboard.addedInformation: The 'worst relay' qualifier makes the irony explicit — a race where every finish line is a grave.
